biomarkers.name: VHL
biomarkers.prevalence: ~70-90% (VHL alteration/inactivation by mutation, deletion, and/or promoter methylation; germline cases are a small minority)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Foundational defining event of ccRCC — leads to HIF stabilisation → VEGF/PDGF upregulation → rationale for anti-angiogenic TKIs. Germline VHL: von Hippel-Lindau syndrome (bilateral/multifocal ccRCC, phaeochromocytoma, haemangioblastoma, pancreatic NET, retinal angioma). Belzutifan (HIF-2α inhibitor) approved for VHL-associated RCC and also used in advanced ccRCC.

biomarkers.name: PBRM1, BAP1, SETD2 (chromatin modifiers)
biomarkers.clinical_use: PBRM1: prognostic and possibly associated with differential response to IO/TKI-based approaches, but not used clinically as a validated predictive biomarker. BAP1: worse prognosis, aggressive. SETD2: adverse prognosis. Combined loss of BAP1 + PBRM1 is a recognized aggressive genotype; BAP1 + SETD2 co-alteration may also indicate aggressive biology but is less established clinically.

biomarkers.name: PD-L1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Not required for IO combinations (nivo/ipi, pembro/axi, nivo/cabo, pembro/lenvatinib all approved regardless); prognostic in some series but not a validated treatment-selection biomarker in ccRCC.

biomarkers.name: IMDC risk score (clinical)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Karnofsky performance status <80%, time from diagnosis to systemic therapy <1 year, anaemia, hypercalcaemia, neutrophilia, thrombocytosis. Favourable / intermediate / poor risk guides systemic therapy selection and stratification; nivo/ipi classically used in intermediate/poor-risk disease.

biomarkers.name: NLR (neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio), CRP, LDH
biomarkers.clinical_use: Inflammatory/prognostic biomarkers used in various RCC risk models; LDH is a component of the older MSKCC model, not the IMDC model.

biomarkers.name: Chromosome 3p loss / 5q gain
biomarkers.prevalence: 3p loss in the large majority of ccRCC; 5q gain is common
biomarkers.clinical_use: Hallmark genomic pattern of ccRCC. 3p loss targets VHL, PBRM1, BAP1, and SETD2 loci and supports lineage-defining biology, though not routinely used alone for treatment selection.

biomarkers.name: TFE3 / TFEB rearrangements
biomarkers.prevalence: Not a hallmark of ccRCC; characteristic of MiT family translocation RCC rather than conventional clear cell RCC
biomarkers.clinical_use: Important differential-diagnostic driver fusion to exclude when morphology overlaps with clear cell RCC.

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Clear/eosinophilic cells with clear cytoplasm (from lipid and glycogen dissolved during processing) arranged in acinar, nested, or alveolar patterns; delicate vasculature
variants: clear cell with sarcomatoid or rhabdoid transformation (worst prognosis)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: WHO/ISUP grade 1-4 (based primarily on nucleolar prominence in grades 1-3; grade 4 includes extreme pleomorphism, multinucleated giant cells, and/or sarcomatoid/rhabdoid differentiation)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Highly variable — often described across angiogenic (VEGF-driven, relatively TKI-responsive) and inflamed/T-effector immune states, although these are not binary categories
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Highly vascular (VHL/HIF/VEGF-driven angiogenesis); minimal desmoplasia; sarcomatoid transformation shows abundant infiltrating immune cells and high IO responsiveness

cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Retains proximal tubule differentiation (PAX8+, CA9+, vimentin+, CD10+) with clear cytoplasm from glycogen and lipid accumulation associated with VHL/HIF-driven metabolic reprogramming
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Sarcomatoid or rhabdoid transformation reflects dedifferentiation/EMT-like programmes and produces highly aggressive disease — often with enhanced IO responsiveness; VHL loss drives constitutive HIF-α stabilization producing a pseudohypoxic state that reprograms cellular metabolism and phenotype
